name: One-dimensional Wasserstein-1 distance
definition: W_1(P,Q)=∫_ℝ |F_P(x)−F_Q(x)| dx, equivalently the minimum expected absolute transport cost over couplings of P and Q.
variables: P,Q real-valued probability distributions; F_P,F_Q cumulative distribution functions; W_1 nonnegative distance
assumptions: Both distributions have finite first absolute moments and use the same measurement scale.
limitations: Sensitive to the measurement scale; this distance alone is not a significance test.
failure_conditions: Incompatible measurement units or undefined first moments
computation: Sort pooled support values and sum interval lengths times the absolute empirical CDF difference; O((n+m) log(n+m)).

source.citation: SciPy maintainers, wasserstein_distance API, definition and references. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.wasserstein_distance.html

application: Describe shifts between distributions of comparable measurements in authorised historical samples.
required_inputs: Two authorised samples or weighted empirical distributions with comparable units and valid masses.
incompatible_methods: Treating an unsigned descriptive distance as a statistical significance result
mechanism_note: Integrates absolute CDF difference rather than the squared CDF difference used in the one-dimensional energy distance identity.

name: Two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test
definition: D_(n,m)=sup_x |F_n(x)−G_m(x)| for the two-sided test of equality of continuous distributions.
variables: F_n,G_m empirical cumulative distribution functions; n,m sample sizes; D statistic in [0,1]
assumptions: Independent samples with independent observations within each sample; usual distribution-free reference assumes continuous null distribution.
limitations: Dependent or discrete observations need a separately justified null reference; a small statistic does not prove equality.
failure_conditions: Unmodelled dependence or applying a continuous null reference to discrete data
computation: Sort pooled observations, update both empirical CDFs at each distinct support point, and retain maximum absolute difference; obtain valid null probability separately.

source.citation: SciPy maintainers, ks_2samp API, two-sided statistic and references. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.ks_2samp.html

application: Assess distribution differences between two comparable independent authorised historical samples.
required_inputs: Two independent samples of the same measurement under a prespecified testing protocol.
incompatible_methods: Treating paired or serially dependent data as independent
mechanism_note: Maximum empirical CDF separation, distinct from the integrated squared CDF discrepancy.
